## Usage

### Installation

Install from [pypi](https://pypi.org/project/dialoghelper/)

``` sh
$ pip install dialoghelper
```

### Documentation

Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub
[repository](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/dialoghelper)’s
[pages](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/).

### Dialog identity and filenames

In a gateway kernel, dialoghelper reaches rustygate through a
`rustygate` comm, so it needs no URL or token. Outside one, it sends
plain HTTP to `JUPYGATE_URL`. Current-session reads, edits, and
execution use `dh_settings['kid']`, initialized from
`JUPYGATE_KERNEL_ID`. The gateway owns the notebook binding, and renames
and restarts keep the kernel id.

Dialog names include `.ipynb` (added when omitted), and a trailing slash
names a folder instead. Relative inputs such as `lesson.ipynb` resolve
against the current dialog’s folder via the gateway; a leading slash, as
in `/project/lesson.ipynb`, addresses the gateway root rather than the
disk root.
[`list_dialogs()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/dialoghelper/core.html#list_dialogs)
defaults to the current notebook’s folder, retaining notebook extensions
and marking folders with a trailing slash.

### Folder-local skills

Solveit activates pyskills from the dialog’s opening folder before
loading its tool layer. Put a public `.py` module or package in a
`_pyskills/` directory there or in an ancestor. Give it a module
docstring. `list_pyskills()` discovers it and ordinary imports load it
without an install or entry-point declaration. The nearest local folder
wins. Changing cwd or moving a live dialog does not change the selected
scope; restart its kernel to use the new location. Function permissions
remain separate from discovery.

## Development

The source notebooks contain the API explanations and examples. Their
dialog operations require a disposable Solveit dialog. Rustygate’s suite
tests message selection, conversion, import and mutation behavior.
